title: Four Personal Agents, Side by Side

zones.label: Grok Bot (SpaceXAI)
zones.summary: Grok Bot is a hosted, always-on agent whose bots share one cloud computer, which makes it the only one here built around a manager bot directing specialists.
facts: Launched August 11, 2026 as an early-beta cloud agent service.
Each user gets one cloud computer with a browser, files, and a terminal, and every one of that user's bots shares it, including its logins.
Safety claims include an Auto Review step for sensitive actions; analysts note that one compromised bot exposes the rest.
Entry price is about $20 a month (Cursor) or $30 (SuperGrok), plus usage billed at token cost; the allowance is unpublished.

zones.label: Dots (OpenAI)
zones.summary: Dots is a personal agent inside ChatGPT that works in the background with its own cloud computer, and it limits what it can do without asking.
facts: Introduced at DevDay on September 29, 2026, powered by GPT-6 Astra.
Each dot has its own cloud computer and browser, and you can open it at any time to watch what it is doing.
Sign-in passwords are not exposed to the model, background research uses read-only access, and you can write custom approval rules.
Reports conflict on price: Engadget says the first dot is free for Pro and Business Premium, while AIMultiple lists $100 a month.

zones.label: Muse (Meta)
zones.summary: Muse is Meta's consumer agent, with the most explicit purchase-approval story and the narrowest work-tool integrations.
facts: Launched September 8, 2026 in the U.S. for users 18 and older, as an app and inside WhatsApp.
Each user's agent runs in its own cloud virtual machine, and you can watch its browser and review an activity log.
A layer called Sentinel allows, blocks, or sends for approval each action, and each purchase needs approval that shows the exact details.
Pricing is a free tier, $20 a month (Power), and $100 a month (Maximum). Training on user data is on by default, with an opt-out.

zones.label: Claude Cowork (Anthropic)
zones.summary: Cowork is the most mature knowledge-work tool here, but it is session-oriented and the least always-on.
facts: Launched in January 2026 and became generally available on April 9, 2026, as a tab inside Claude Desktop.
It works mostly in a local sandbox plus plugins and MCP connectors. A March 2026 source says scheduled tasks need the computer awake and Claude Desktop open.
There is no separate price: it is included in Claude Pro ($20), Max ($100 or $200), Team, and Enterprise plans, sharing one usage pool with chat and Claude Code.
Enterprise adds role-based access control and spend limits, but one source notes Cowork activity is not yet in audit logs.

quiz.question: Which agent has every one of a user's bots sharing a single cloud computer and its logins?
quiz.explanation: Grok Bot gives each user one cloud computer, so one compromised bot exposes the rest.

quiz.question: Which agent introduced at DevDay hides sign-in passwords from the model and lets you write your own approval rules?
quiz.explanation: Dots keeps passwords away from the underlying model and supports custom approval rules.

quiz.question: Which agent uses a layer called Sentinel and needs approval showing exact details for each purchase?
quiz.explanation: Muse's Sentinel layer allows, blocks, or sends each action for approval.

quiz.question: Which agent is the least always-on, because one source says scheduled tasks need the computer awake?
quiz.explanation: Cowork lives in Claude Desktop, so a March 2026 source says it needs the computer awake.

quiz.question: Which agent's price is reported inconsistently, from free to $100 a month?
quiz.explanation: Engadget and AIMultiple disagree, so check OpenAI's own announcement.

quiz.question: Which agent is included in the $20 to $200 Claude plans rather than sold separately?
quiz.explanation: Cowork has no separate SKU and draws on the same usage pool as Claude chat and Claude Code.
